title: Terminal hotkey passthrough and focus on activate
why: Two edits to the terminal bundle. The plugin has no setting for either edit. (1) Hotkey passthrough. When a terminal has focus, the plugin replaces the Obsidian hotkey table with a fixed allow list. The edit adds these command ids to the list, so that their hotkeys still reach Obsidian: open a new terminal, open the settings, the Vertical Tabs zen mode, go to tab 1 to 8, go to the last tab, close, next tab, previous tab, the quick switcher, and the command palette. hotkeys.json holds the Alt+Ctrl+T binding itself. (2) Focus on activate. Upstream, the active-leaf-change handler only records the last leaf that is not a terminal. It never moves focus into a terminal whose leaf becomes active, so a tab-switch hotkey leaves the keyboard focus outside the terminal input. The edit calls the focus() method of the terminal view when its leaf becomes active. A guard allows the focus move only while the Obsidian window has the focus. The guard reads isFocused() of the Electron BrowserWindow, and it uses document.hasFocus() only when Electron is not available. On Wayland, document.hasFocus() stays true when the window does not have the focus, and a focus call then makes Hyprland raise Obsidian above the current app.
